title: Institutional FX Dashboard & Intelligence Report — July 15, 2026

regime.classification: Relief Rally, still shadowed by war risk — Asian and early-European markets extended yesterday's cool-CPI relief overnight even as the Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis produced its most geographically widespread single night of the crisis yet.
regime.justification: Asian equities rallied broadly overnight, tracking Wall Street's Tuesday gains on the soft June CPI print — South Korea's KOSPI surged 6.2% to 7,284.41 (a sharp rebound from a recent semiconductor-led sell-off), Japan's Nikkei 225 rose roughly 1.3% to 68,613.89 (a separate read shows +0.9% to 68,353.91), Australia's ASX 200 gained 0.4% to 8,841.10, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng added 1.5% to 24,701.10, while mainland China's Shanghai Composite slipped 0.2% to 3,957.79. Markets are now pricing well-reduced odds of a September Fed hike (one read puts it below 17%, down sharply from prior levels) — a materially more dovish market read than Chair Warsh's own hawkish-leaning testimony yesterday would suggest, a genuine and still-unresolved tension heading into his second testimony (Senate Banking Committee) later today. Overnight, the Iran/Hormuz crisis widened further: fresh US strikes were conducted at dawn "to continue degrading Iranian capabilities," while Iran retaliated simultaneously across three US-allied states — Jordan's air defenses intercepted three ballistic missiles at dawn, Kuwait's Air Defence Forces intercepted six missiles and 33 drones (with a Kuwaiti Navy vessel hit and four sailors wounded), and Bahrain intercepted a further wave of aerial attacks and sounded air-raid sirens. Oil extended its rally for a third consecutive session (Brent above $85, its highest levels of the crisis), while gold eased modestly (~$4,037-4,044/oz, -0.4%) even against this backdrop — a continuation of the "safe-haven paradox" this crisis has produced since its early days.
regime.executiveSummary: This is a genuinely two-track morning. The market-facing story is optimistic: yesterday's cool US CPI print is still working its way through risk assets, with Asian equities — led by an outsized KOSPI rebound — extending Wall Street's gains and rates markets pricing a much lower probability of a September hike than Chair Warsh's own rhetoric implied in his House testimony yesterday. That divergence between market pricing and the Fed chair's own messaging is itself a live, unresolved risk heading into today's Senate testimony. The geopolitical story is more alarming: overnight brought the most simultaneously widespread Iranian retaliation of the entire crisis, striking three separate US-allied states within hours of each other, alongside a fresh round of US strikes. Markets have so far treated this as a commodity story (oil higher for a third straight session) rather than a broad risk-off trigger — equities are rallying, not falling, even as the war escalates. Today brings two major, still-pending catalysts: the Bank of Canada's rate decision (9:45am ET; virtually unanimous expectation of a hold at 2.25%, alongside a fresh Monetary Policy Report) and Chair Warsh's second congressional appearance in two days, this time before a Senate Banking Committee with several crypto-focused members, where markets will be watching for any dovish softening — or hawkish reinforcement — of yesterday's message.

**Educational Breakdown — Long NZD/USD (final entry, closed full win):**

*What we expected, and why:* Published 4 Jul, the thesis was short-covering plus a hawkish RBNZ repricing building into the 8 Jul decision. At publication it scored 65/100 overall, with Positioning as the strongest relative signal (15/20 — NZD shorts had already unwound to a 6-month low) and Macro contributing the most raw points (24/35 — "RBNZ pivot narrative building but decision still ahead"). Technicals were deliberately weak (14/25 — "lagging peers on spot, no fresh breakout confirmed"), and the report named an explicit, dated confirmation trigger: watch the 8 Jul RBNZ statement for hawkish language before adding.

*What actually happened:* The RBNZ delivered exactly that trigger — a 25bp hike on 8 Jul, its first in three years. That single dated event became a genuinely durable, eight-session catalyst: NZD/USD ground from the ~0.5655 entry midpoint through the first target (0.5750, hit ~13 Jul) and on to the second (0.5820, hit intraday 14 Jul), closing the idea out.

*Match or divergence — and why:* This matched, cleanly. The most predictive element wasn't the raw macro score (a middling 24/35 at publication) — it was the combination of already-unwound positioning (nowhere left for shorts to cover) plus a specific, dated event the report told readers to watch for. When a thesis names an exact confirmation trigger rather than a vague "bullish backdrop," and positioning has already cleared out the crowded side of the trade, the setup tends to have real follow-through once the trigger fires. The weak Technicals score at publication (14/25) wasn't a warning sign here — it was simply too early; technical confirmation followed the fundamental catalyst rather than leading it. This is the tracker's first fully closed idea, and the cleanest teaching example so far of a thesis playing out exactly as the original reasoning predicted.

**Running Hit Rate: 1 played out (closed — full, double-target win) / 0 invalidated / 3 still pending, out of 4 total ideas issued since July 4, 2026 (first-run date of the merged structure).** With Long NZD/USD now formally closed, Short AUD/NZD becomes the clearest candidate for the tracker's second win — a confirmed close through 1.1950 at the next run would extend the hit rate to 2 of 4.

sections.title: Contrarian Check & Risks
sections.raw:
**Primary thesis risk:** The gap between market pricing (sub-17% odds of a September Fed hike) and Chair Warsh's own hawkish rhetoric is the report's most important unresolved tension — today's Senate Banking Committee testimony could resolve it sharply in either direction. Separately, the Iran/Hormuz crisis's widening geographic footprint (three separate US-allied states struck overnight) raises the tail risk of a genuine risk-off shock that overwhelms the current relief-rally tone, even though markets have not priced that outcome so far.

**Overall-view invalidation factor:** A hawkish reinforcement from Warsh's Senate testimony today, combined with any confirmed further widening of the Iran/Hormuz conflict (rather than the current pattern of contained, intercepted strikes), would be the cleanest scenario to reverse today's risk-on tone and pressure both this report's open ideas.

- **Bull case (for this report's ideas):** AUD/NZD is confirmed to have closed through its first target (1.1950) once fresh data arrives; a dovish surprise from Warsh's Senate testimony finally gives the USD/JPY short thesis a genuine catalyst. *Invalidated by:* a confirmed, sustained break of 163.50 in USD/JPY or 1.2250 in AUD/NZD.
- **Base case:** AUD/NZD is confirmed to remain just above its first target without a close through it; USD/JPY holds broadly within its recent range through today's BoC decision and Warsh testimony. *Invalidated by:* a decisive break in either pair's key level.
- **Bear case:** A hawkish surprise from Warsh's Senate testimony reverses the current risk-on tone, USD/JPY grinds back toward its highs, and AUD/NZD bounces back above 1.2100 as the overnight NZD strength fades. *Invalidated by:* continued dollar softness and a confirmed AUD/NZD close through 1.1950.
